data.title: 100kg boar takes a stroll along the highway
data.description: A 100-kilogramme "wild boar" let out of its pen for a walk instead wandered off onto a nearby elevated highway, startling motorists and disrupting traffic on Monday. His owner took more than an hour to sweet-talk him into returning home.

data.title: Chinese artist sentenced to three years in prison for Mao sculptures
data.description: NEW YORK — A Chinese court on Tuesday sentenced a prominent New York-based artist, Gao Zhen, to three years in prison for making irreverent sculptures of Mao Zedong more than 15 years ago, according to his wife.

data.description: South Korean police are hunting five suspects believed to have fled to Thailand for allegedly operating an illegal gambling site involving 60 billion won (1.5 billion baht).

data.title: Namibia paves way for phosphate mining in the Atlantic Ocean
data.description: WINDHOEK — Namibia has granted environmental clearance for an offshore phosphate mining project that paves the way for the world's first commercial seabed-dredging operation for the mineral, despite opposition from green groups and the fishing industry.

data.title: Cabinet to extend social security cover to farm, street, domestic workers
data.description: The Labour Ministry will propose an expansion of social security coverage under Section 33 to include agricultural workers, street vendors and domestic workers.

data.title: Southern border rail track reopens after bombing
data.description: NARATHIWAT - Train services have resumed on the main southern line in Rangae district, following repairs, after it was damaged by a bomb on Saturday night, the State Railway of Thailand said on Tuesday.

data.title: High-tides alert for six central provinces, Bangkok
data.description: Low-lying areas in six central provinces and Bangkok have been warned to prepare for possible flooding caused by very high tides from Tuesday to Saturday this week.

data.title: Florida opens a dedicated Jellyfish Museum
data.description: Right on the coast of Florida, Pompano Beach has opened a new venture dedicated to one of the ocean’s most enigmatic creatures: the jellyfish, a boneless and brainless invertebrate that has survived in the earth’s ocean for over 500 million years.

data.title: Illegal hookah shop shut down in Phuket
data.description: PHUKET - Authorities have seized 32 illegal hookah sets, known as “Baragu” in Thai, from a shop in Muang district that caters to tourists.

data.title: Convenience store bombed in deep South as two suspects arrested
data.description: PATTANI — Another convenience store was bombed and set ablaze in the deep South, while two suspects were arrested after a brief gunfight in this southern border province on Monday night.

data.title: Eight styles of Chud Thai take centre stage at Tokyo National Museum
data.description: Thailand will showcase all eight styles of Chud Thai Phra Ratchaniyom, royal-court craftsmanship and specialist lectures in Tokyo on September 17-18.

data.title: Six months into Iran war, Hormuz traffic way down, sailors stranded
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Six months since the start of the Middle East war, the strategic Strait of Hormuz remains largely paralysed, with thousands of sailors still stranded in the Gulf and commodity carrier traffic way below its normal level.

data.title: Cool Japan: Human fridge chills workers in extreme heat
data.description: TOKYO — Feeling dizzy and unwell after cycling to work in Japan's punishing summer heat, warehouse worker Isao Tabuchi headed for his company's newest acquisition: a refrigerator for humans.
